Inferencia bayesiana

Author

Bernardo L. Español

Librerías y datos

library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(brms)
df <- read_delim("usu_individual_T125.txt", delim=";")

df <- df %>%
  rename(
    "age" = "CH06",
    "salary" = "P21"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    salary > 0,
    ESTADO == 1,
    between(age, 18, 40)
  ) %>%
  arrange(age) %>%
  select("age", "salary")
df
df_mean <- df %>% 
  group_by(age) %>%
  summarise(
    salary_mean = mean(salary),
    salary_var = var(salary)
  ) %>%
  arrange(age)
df_mean

Regresión lineal

Para el salario

ggplot(df, aes(x = age, y = salary)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "Edad", y = "Salario") +
  theme_minimal()
mod_lm <- lm(formula = salary ~ age, data = df)
tidy(mod_lm)
ggplot(df_mean, aes(x = age, y = salary_mean))+
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_abline(
    intercept = coef(mod_lm)[1],
    slope = coef(mod_lm)[2],
    linewidth = 1.2, col = "#C95E61"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

Para el modelo lineal (normal, i. e. no bayesiano) la predicción es puntual:

predict(mod_lm, newdata = data.frame(age = 30),
        interval = "prediction", level = 0.68)
       fit      lwr     upr
1 670307.2 24580.05 1316034

Para log(salario)

ggplot(df, aes(x = age, y = salary)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  theme_minimal()
mod_lm_log <- lm(formula = log(salary) ~ age, data = df)
tidy(mod_lm_log)
ggplot(df, aes(x = age, y = log(salary)))+
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_abline(
      intercept = coef(mod_lm_log)[1],
      slope = coef(mod_lm_log)[2],
      linewidth = 1.2, col = "#C95E61"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

Modelo lineal bayesiano

\Pr(\theta \mid y)= \frac{\Pr(y \mid \theta)\,\Pr(\theta)}{\Pr(y)}\propto \Pr(y \mid \theta)\,\Pr(\theta). 

mod_brm_default <- brm(salary ~ age, data = df, refresh = 0)
mod_brm_default
 Family: gaussian 
  Links: mu = identity 
Formula: salary ~ age 
   Data: df (Number of observations: 7866) 
  Draws: 4 chains, each with iter = 2000; warmup = 1000; thin = 1;
         total post-warmup draws = 4000

Regression Coefficients:
          Estimate Est.Error  l-95% CI  u-95% CI Rhat Bulk_ESS Tail_ESS
Intercept 59106.37  39092.48 -17222.68 134633.61 1.00     3808     2836
age       20374.24   1251.78  17924.38  22788.04 1.00     3793     2604

Further Distributional Parameters:
       Estimate Est.Error  l-95% CI  u-95% CI Rhat Bulk_ESS Tail_ESS
sigma 649263.26   5182.22 639007.73 659540.93 1.00     4497     3178

Draws were sampled using sampling(NUTS). For each parameter, Bulk_ESS
and Tail_ESS are effective sample size measures, and Rhat is the potential
scale reduction factor on split chains (at convergence, Rhat = 1).
plot(mod_brm_default)

Predicción para los valores medios del modelo

b <- fixef(mod_brm_default)

ggplot(df_mean, aes(x = age, y = salary_mean)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_abline(
    intercept = b["Intercept","Estimate"],
    slope     = b["age","Estimate"],
    col = "#C95E61",
    linewidth = 1.2,
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

También podemos usar brms::conditional_effects() para graficar la predicción:

ce <- conditional_effects(mod_brm_default)
p  <- plot(ce, plot = FALSE)[[1]]
p + geom_point(data = df_mean, aes(x = age, y = salary_mean), alpha = 0.8, inherit.aes = FALSE)  + theme_minimal()

Posterior para diferente cantidad de muestras

get_prior(mod_brm_default)
sizes <- c(100, 500, 2000, nrow(df))
set.seed(1)

get_post_long <- function(n) {
  idx <- sample.int(nrow(df), n)
  fit <- brm(salary ~ age, data = df[idx, ], refresh = 0)
  d <- as_draws_df(fit)[, c("b_Intercept", "b_age", "sigma")]
  long <- stack(d)
  long$n <- n
  long
}

posteriors_long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sizes, get_post_long))
ggplot(posteriors_long, aes(x = values, color = factor(n))) +
  geom_density() +
  facet_wrap(~ ind, scales = "free", ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Posterior", y = "Density", color = "n") +
  theme_minimal()

Predicción para una edad determinada

age_eval = 30
ggplot(data = filter(df, age == age_eval), aes(x = salary)) + geom_density() + theme_minimal()
draws <- as_draws_df(mod_brm_default)
mu <- draws$b_Intercept + age_eval * draws$b_age # linear prediction
age_eval_draws <- rnorm(length(mu), mu, draws$sigma)

ggplot(data = data.frame(x = age_eval_draws), aes(x = x)) + geom_density() + theme_minimal()

o directamente usando la función brms::posterior_predict()

plot_age_posterior_predict <- function(model, age){
  salary_draws_for_one_age <- posterior_predict(
    model,
    newdata = data.frame(age = age),
    ndraws = 4000,
  )[,1]

  ggplot(data = data.frame(x = salary_draws_for_one_age), aes(x = x)) + geom_density() + theme_minimal()
}
plot_age_posterior_predict(mod_brm_default, age = 30)

Predicción para todas las edades

pp_check(mod_brm_default)

Vemos que los valores medios están bien representados, pero la distribución de la predicción del posterior no.

Modelo bayesiano con otra función para la verosimilitud (familia y enlace)

y \sim \text{Normal}(\mu, \sigma),\quad \mu = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x \quad\longrightarrow\quad y \sim \text{Gamma}(\mu, \alpha),\quad \log(\mu) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x 

mod_brm_family_gamma <- brm(
  salary ~ age, data = df,
  family = Gamma("log"),
  refresh = 0
)
mod_brm_family_gamma
 Family: gamma 
  Links: mu = log 
Formula: salary ~ age 
   Data: df (Number of observations: 7866) 
  Draws: 4 chains, each with iter = 2000; warmup = 1000; thin = 1;
         total post-warmup draws = 4000

Regression Coefficients:
          Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Rhat Bulk_ESS Tail_ESS
Intercept    12.43      0.05    12.34    12.52 1.00     5273     3057
age           0.03      0.00     0.03     0.04 1.00     5370     3089

Further Distributional Parameters:
      Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Rhat Bulk_ESS Tail_ESS
shape     1.88      0.03     1.83     1.94 1.00     2077     2212

Draws were sampled using sampling(NUTS). For each parameter, Bulk_ESS
and Tail_ESS are effective sample size measures, and Rhat is the potential
scale reduction factor on split chains (at convergence, Rhat = 1).
plot(mod_brm_family_gamma)
b <- fixef(mod_brm_family_gamma)

ggplot(df, aes(x = age, y = log(salary))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.35, size = 1.2) +
  geom_abline(
    intercept = b["Intercept","Estimate"],
    slope     = b["age","Estimate"],
    col = "#C95E61",
    linewidth = 1.2,
  ) + theme_minimal()
plot_age_posterior_predict(mod_brm_family_gamma, 30)
pp_check(mod_brm_family_gamma)

Otras ventajas del modelo bayesiano

library(lme4)

data("sleepstudy", package = "lme4")
data = sleepstudy
lab <- levels(sleepstudy$Subject)
lab_map <- setNames(paste("Sujeto", seq_along(lab)), lab)

ggplot(sleepstudy, aes(x = Days, y = Reaction, group = Subject)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ Subject, nrow = 6, ncol = 3,
             labeller = labeller(Subject = lab_map)) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Días", y = "Reacción (ms)")
mod <- brm(Reaction ~ Days, data = data, refresh = 0)
conditional_effects(mod)
mod_conditioned <- brm(Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject), data = data, refresh = 0)
conditional_effects(mod_conditioned)
